newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called lower after Wed. rise.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called lower after Wed. rise.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open lower Thursday after rising Wednesday on an unplanned outage at the 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear power unit in central California.
"People want this market to come off after the recent run-up," a Houston futures trader said.

In over-the-counter business, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $34.10-34.40 a megawatt hour, below Wednesday's settlement at $34.65, and August California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $22.80-23.25 lower than yesterday's close at $23.30.
On the downside, analysts assessed technical support for August PV near $33.30 and August COB $22.00-22.60.

Diablo Canyon 2 was taken off line early Wednesday due to a problem in the feedwater system. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission indicated the unit could restart as early as today if the root cause of the problem were found.
Ahead of the July 4th holiday weekend, PV futures are scheduled to stop trading at 1255 EDT and COB at 1300 EDT today, two and a half hour earlier than normal.
NYMEX will also be closed Friday.

The 1,070 MW San Onofre 2 nuclear unit remained shut last Sunday to replace its charge line check valves, and the 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 has been out of service since April 12 for refueling and maintenance.
San Onofre units 2 and 3 were expected to resume operation around July 15 and July 10, respectively.
In addition, capacity at the 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 nuclear unit near Phoenix, Ariz., has been trimmed Wednesday by 15 percent for repair work expected to take 24 hours.

Meteorologists called for a warming trend to begin later this week in the Pacific Northwest following recent cooler-than-normal weather. Meanwhile, forecasts called for temperatures in the Southwest to stay near to above normal through next week.
